q: 1. Quick lime is a .....
options: product left immediately after the calcinations of pure limestone
explain: Quick lime is the product left immediately after calcination of limestone. Although chemically it is CaO, the answer key gives option c.

q: 2. After the addition of water to it, the cement sets and hardens due to .....
options: the heat produced by the chemical action
the hydration and hydrolysis of the constituent compounds of cement
explain: Cement sets and hardens by hydration and hydrolysis of its compounds (C3S, C2S, C3A, C4AF), forming a rigid gel.

q: 3. The consistency test is performed to find .....
explain: The consistency test (Vicat) finds the water percentage that gives a paste of standard consistency, used for setting time and soundness tests.

q: 4. For normal consistency, the penetration in Vicat apparatus should be between .....
explain: Standard consistency is reached when the plunger stops 5 to 7 mm from the bottom, i.e. penetrates about 33 to 35 mm of the 40 mm mould.

q: 5. In briquette test, the seven day tensile strength of good Portland cement should not be less than .....
explain: The seven-day tensile strength of a good Portland cement briquette should be at least 25 kg/cm².

q: 6. The seven day compressive strength of a good Portland cement, as obtained from the compressive test on cement-sand mortar cubes, should not be less than .....
explain: The seven-day compressive strength of cement-sand mortar cubes should be at least 175 kg/cm² (about 17.5 MPa).

q: 7. The final setting time of ordinary Portland cement should not be less than .....
explain: As per the answer key, option c (10 h). Note: the usual code limit is that final setting time should not be MORE than 10 hours, so this question is worded oddly in the book.

q: 8. Quick setting cement is used .....
options: for the construction of structures under water
where resistance to acidic water is required
explain: Quick setting cement sets fast, so it is used for underwater work and in running water where the cement must set before being washed away.

q: 9. The initial and final setting times of quick setting cement are .....
explain: Quick setting cement has an initial setting time of about 5 minutes and a final setting time of about 30 minutes.

q: 10. The pozzolona portland cement gains the strength .....
options: in the same time as ordinary Portland cement
in less time than ordinary Portland cement
In more time than ordinary Portland cement
explain: Pozzolanic reaction with lime is slow, so pozzolana Portland cement gains strength more slowly than ordinary Portland cement.

q: 11. In the chemical composition test for loss on ignition, the cement is heated to a temperature of .....
explain: In the loss on ignition test the cement sample is ignited at about 1000°C to drive off moisture and CO2.

q: 12. Excessive free lime and excessive magnesia present in the cement make the cement .....
options: to have very low initial setting time
to have very low compressive strength
explain: Free lime and magnesia hydrate slowly after setting and expand, causing cracks and disintegration; such cement is unsound.

q: 13. Snowcem is .....
explain: Snowcem is a proprietary cement-based paint (coloured cement) used for exterior wall finishing. It is the closest option here.

q: 14. For the manufacture of Portland cement, the proportions of raw materials used, are
explain: Portland cement raw materials are proportioned at roughly 63% lime, 22% silica, and 15% other ingredients.

q: 15. Good quality cement contains higher percentage of
explain: A higher proportion of tricalcium silicate (C3S) gives cement better early strength and overall quality.

q: 16. In the cement the compound quickest to react with water, is
explain: Tricalcium aluminate (C3A) reacts almost instantly with water, causing flash set if not controlled by gypsum.

q: 17. Rapid hardening cement contains
explain: Rapid hardening cement has a higher C3S content, which speeds up early strength development.

q: 18. Ultimate strength to cement is provided by
explain: Dicalcium silicate (C2S) hydrates slowly and provides the long-term ultimate strength of cement.

q: 19. To retard the initial setting time of cement, the compound responsible, is
explain: Gypsum is added during grinding to slow down the fast reaction of C3A, retarding initial setting.

q: 20. The compound of Portland cement which reacts immediately with water and also sets first is
explain: Tricalcium aluminate (C3A) reacts with water immediately and is the first compound to set.

q: 21. The commonly used raw material in the manufacture of cement, is
explain: Limestone is the principal raw material, supplying the calcium required for cement manufacture.

q: 22. The percentage of water required for normal consistency for OPC cement, is
explain: For OPC, the standard consistency test typically requires water content between 26% and 33% by weight of cement.

q: 23. For slaking of 10 kg of CaO, the theoretical amount of water is .....
explain: CaO + H2O gives Ca(OH)2. Molar masses are 56 and 18, so water needed = 10 × 18/56 ≈ 3.2 kg.

q: 24. Apparatus for Soundness test of cement is
explain: Le Chatelier's apparatus measures cement paste expansion, used to determine soundness.

q: 25. Pick up the compound responsible for early strength of cement from the following .....
explain: Tricalcium silicate (C3S) hydrates quickly and gives the early strength (up to about 7 days). C3A causes flash set but contributes little strength.

q: 26. Soundness test of cement determines
explain: The soundness test checks for excess free lime or magnesia, which can cause delayed expansion and cracking.

q: 27. The percentage of the residue left after sieving good Portland cement in 90 micron sieve should not exceed .....
explain: For fineness, the residue on a 90 micron IS sieve should not exceed 10%.

q: 28. The ability of cement to maintain a constant volume is called
explain: Soundness is defined as cement's ability to retain a constant volume after setting without expansion.

q: 29. The expansion in portland cement can be tested by .....
explain: The soundness test (Le Chatelier apparatus or autoclave) measures expansion due to free lime and magnesia.

q: 30. The compressive strength of a good Portland cement and standards and mortar after 3 days of curing should not be less than .....
explain: As per the older IS, the 3-day compressive strength of standard mortar should not be less than 11.5 MN/m².

q: 31. White cement should have least percentage of
explain: Iron oxide imparts grey/brown color to ordinary cement, so white cement is made with minimal iron oxide.

q: 32. The sand is mixed with lime mortar to .....
explain: Sand is an inert filler that reduces shrinkage and cracking of lime mortar and makes it porous so CO2 can reach it.

q: 33. The insoluble residue in cement is less than
explain: Specifications limit the insoluble residue (impurities) in cement to less than about 1.5%.

q: 34. For a 50 kg cement bag water required, is
explain: For a standard 50 kg cement bag, about 22.5 litres of water is typically used based on standard mix proportions.

q: 35. Which of the following rocks is used in cement manufacturing?
explain: Limestone supplies the calcium oxide (lime) which is the main raw material for cement.

q: 36. Quick lime is
explain: Quicklime is chemically calcium oxide (CaO), produced by burning (calcining) limestone.

q: 37. The silicious and aluminous minerals, which do not have cementitious qualities by themselves but which react with lime in the presence of water at normal temperature to form cementitious compounds, are known as
explain: Pozzolanic materials react chemically with lime and water at ordinary temperature to form cementitious compounds.

q: 38. The aggregate is called fine aggregate if it is completely retained on .....
explain: As per the answer key, option a. Note: fine aggregate is usually defined as passing 4.75 mm and retained on 0.15 mm, so the wording in the book is loose.

q: 39. The aggregate is called coarse aggregate if it is completely retained on .....
explain: Aggregate retained on the 4.75 mm IS sieve is coarse aggregate. (The book prints option d with an 's)' label.)

q: 40. The sand in mortar
options: helps the pure lime to set by allowing penetration of air which provides the needed carbon dioxide
explain: Sand serves multiple functions in mortar: bulking the volume, reducing shrinkage/cracking, and allowing air (CO2) to penetrate for lime carbonation.

q: 41. The bulking of sand is due to .....
options: the increase in space between the particles, caused by the surface tension effect of moisture
the swelling of air in voids
explain: A thin film of moisture around sand particles pushes them apart through surface tension, increasing the volume (bulking).

q: 42. The cement mortar mix generally used for masonry work is .....
explain: As per the answer key, a 1:6 cement-sand mortar is generally used for masonry work.

q: 43. The volume of one bag of cement weighing 50 kg is
explain: A standard 50 kg bag of cement occupies a volume of about 0.0345 cubic meters, based on cement's bulk density.

q: 44. The cement mortar mix generally used for internal plastering is .....
explain: As per the answer key, a 1:5 mix is generally used for internal plastering.

q: 45. Stucco are suitable for .....
explain: Stucco is a plaster finish that can be applied on both stone masonry and brick walls.

q: 46. A mortar prepared by mixing wood powder or saw dust to the cement or lime mortar is known as
explain: Adding lightweight fillers like sawdust or wood powder to mortar produces light weight mortar.

q: 47. Ultimate strength to cement is provided by .....
explain: Dicalcium silicate (C2S) hydrates slowly and is responsible for the later (ultimate) strength.

q: 48. According to air permeability method of fineness test of cement, the specific surface expressed in cm2/gm of a good Portland cement should not be less than
explain: As per the air permeability (Blaine) method, good Portland cement should have a specific surface of at least about 2250 cm2/gm.

q: 49. To retard the initial setting time of cement, the compound responsible, is .....
explain: Gypsum is added (about 2 to 3%) to control the quick setting caused by C3A.

q: 50. The compound of Portland cement which reacts immediately with water and also sets first is .....
explain: Tricalcium aluminate (C3A) reacts instantly with water and causes flash set.
